newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end week of records mainly stable.
newsitem.headline: German shares end week of records mainly stable.

text.p: German shares held mainly steady after a week of record highs on Friday, as many market players extended the Ascension Thursday holiday into a long weekend, lowering volumes appreciably.

Firm Bunds, strong futures and an upbeat overnight close on Wall Street underpinned sentiment over the bourse session and the blue chip DAX index ended up 10.43 points, or 0.29 percent, at 3,562.41 points.
"We are holding on well here even though the dollar is weaker. It is stable, at least," said a Frankfurt trader.
Prices eased in the late post-bourse session, with the IBIS DAX closing down 4.24 points at 3,533.21 points as the dollar continued to weaken, falling to below 1.69 marks in late share trade.
After the DAX's sharp ascent of the past weeks, a lull was inevitable, dealers said.
"In the short term the market appears overbought after the steep rise of the past weeks," said Bayerische Vereinsbank's research team.
Despite a licking in recent days from the yen and other currencies, the dollar was still seen as having a positive impact on the German share market in the mid-term.

Among the few features of the session was airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG, which ended bourse trade up 1.25 marks, 4.65 percent, at 28.10 marks, still riding a wave of positive sentiment after upbeat first-quarter 1997 figures on Wednesday.
Lufthansa held its gains later to close IBIS dealings at 28.09 marks.

Shares in electronics giant Siemens AG hit 100 marks for the first time ever, and the share ended at a closing high of 100.10 marks, a rise of 2.65 marks or 2.69 percent, boosted by news of new orders from New Zealand.
Siemens ended the IBIS day at 100.90 marks.
